conventions.convention: M0(w) uses nondecreasing weights w_l ≥ 1 and a weighted supremum norm with normalized level maxima tending to zero. Admissibility means w_l/√l → ∞. The extra Haar scaling coordinate has weight 1 and is retained by finite projections.
The primitive map additionally requires summability of ∑ w_l 2^(-l/2), together with the stated wavelet cancellation and localization assumptions; admissibility alone does not supply this.

Smooth white-noise functionals use a nonzero representer g in the basis Sobolev space H2^s with s > 1/2. Evaluation at the observation means the continuous negative-Sobolev coefficient pairing, not an L² inner product with an L²-valued observation.

Type-S1 uses globally log-Lipschitz coefficient densities and scales 2^(-l(α+1/2)), with α > 1. Type-S2 uses Gaussian coefficients, α > 1/2, and 0 < r < α - 1/4. Type H uses Haar histograms, 1/2 < α ≤ 1, and positive Dirichlet parameters between c1 2^(-L_n a) and c2.

Type S retains wavelet levels through L_n; a type-H histogram at resolution L_n retains its scaling coordinate and details l < L_n. The allowed cutoffs are the largest integers below n^(1/(2α+1)) or (n/log n)^(1/(2α+1)) on the dyadic scale.
Quantile stabilization requires a continuous limiting CDF and strict increase on an open neighborhood of the particular lower quantile; global strict increase on the real line is unnecessary.
The nonlinear theorem explicitly assumes contraction of the L² norm itself at radius r_n = o(n^(-1/2)), rather than contraction of its square at that rate.

Density calibration requires both posterior BvM about the chosen center and a sampling CLT for that same center, with the same Gaussian bridge law. Posterior credibility means mass at least the nominal level; coverage tends to the nominal level.
The white-noise functional results inherit countable choice. The density posterior BvM, Gaussian bridge, sampling CLT, and source-specific calibration results explicitly assume full AC.

load_bearing.statement: For data-indexed probability measures Q_n and a fixed probability G on M0(w), bounded-Lipschitz convergence in probability of every fixed finite projection, together with the stated iterated posterior-tail condition for every ε,η > 0, implies bounded-Lipschitz convergence of Q_n to G in probability.

Under its stated AC, Type-S prior, bounded positive truth, smoothness, basis, and cutoff hypotheses, posterior quotient log-density coordinates contract around θ_* at radius e_n = √(d/n) + d^(-α), in the sense that their errors divided by e_n are tight in probability. The posterior normalizer is positive and finite almost surely, and the quotient prior has the stated positive continuous density and translation bounds.

Assume AC and all stated Type-S1 or Type-S2 truth, basis, prior-scale, and cutoff hypotheses. For every admissible w, the posterior law of √n(f - P_n(L_n)) converges in bounded-Lipschitz distance on M0(w), in P0^n-probability, to the Borel Gaussian bridge with covariance P0[(ψ_i - P0ψ_i)(ψ_j - P0ψ_j)].

Assume AC and the original stated Type-H conditions, including 1/2 < α ≤ 1, bounded positive C^α truth, either cutoff, and the displayed Dirichlet-parameter bounds. For every nondecreasing admissible w, the posterior law of √n(f - h_n) converges in bounded-Lipschitz distance on M0(w), in P0^n-probability, to the Borel Gaussian bridge; its scaling coordinate is zero.

Assume AC, a bounded sampling density with the stated wavelet coefficient decay at order γ > 1/2, the stated wavelet bounds, admissible w, either cutoff regime, and the specified Borel Gaussian bridge law. Then √n(P_n(L_n) - f0) converges weakly to that bridge in M0(w).

Under AC, bounded positive density, complete wavelet basis, admissible weights, and the stated primitive-map geometry and summability hypotheses, the CDFs of the multiscale bridge norm and its primitive supremum norm are continuous on the real line, strictly increasing on positive arguments, zero at zero, and strictly between zero and one at every positive argument.

Under its stated density, wavelet, primitive-map, posterior BvM, sampling-center CLT, and positive locally unique continuous norm-quantile hypotheses, the centered root-n CDF posterior converges to the P0-Brownian bridge, the posterior norm balls are measurable credible sets, their frequentist coverage tends to 1 - α, and their scaled radii converge to the corresponding limit quantiles.

If data-indexed scalar probability kernels converge in bounded-Lipschitz distance in probability to a fixed law with continuous CDF, and that CDF is strictly increasing on an open interval containing its lower u-quantile for 0 < u < 1, then the corresponding posterior lower quantiles converge in probability.

Under its explicit compact multiresolution hypotheses, the projection kernels have uniformly bounded integral norms and localized support, multiplication by a β-Hölder function commutes with projection up to C 2^(-βL) times the supremum norm on V_L, and the stated additional derivative and cancellation hypotheses give coefficient approximation and exponential composition at every positive α, including integer α.

concerns.concern: The Statement assumes an L² radius 'r_n=o(n^(-1/2))' while retaining the product-prior weak BvM and a nonzero smooth representer. These hypotheses are incompatible, so the conditional theorem is vacuous, although its implication is logically valid. Indeed, contraction makes √n L_g(f-f0) converge to zero in posterior probability. Consequently the modulus of its posterior characteristic function tends to 1. Translating by √n L_g(X-f0) leaves that modulus unchanged, whereas the scalar consequence of weak BvM forces it to tend to exp(-t²||g||²/2) < 1 for t ≠ 0. The paragraph calling this merely a 'stronger convention' should disclose this caveat. The cited [Castillo–Nickl Theorem 4, printed p. 2011](https://www.statslab.cam.ac.uk/~rn289/Site/__files/AOS1133.pdf#page=13) instead places o(n^(-1/2)) on the squared L² radius.

The Statement says, 'In particular the CDF posterior converges in bounded-Lipschitz distance to the P0-Brownian bridge law.' The cited calibration theorem establishes this for the posterior law of √n(F_f - F_T_n), not for the uncentered CDF posterior. The centering and root-n scaling need to be explicit in this sentence; the proof invokes the correctly transformed result. The distinction is also explicit in equation (1) of the [cited density paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1310.2484#page=2).

The Type-S2 paragraph says 'its source theorem uses ... α>1/2'. The cited [Castillo–Nickl density paper, Theorem 3](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1310.2484#page=14) assumes α>1 for type S, including its Gaussian case. Equations (23)–(24) define prior regimes more broadly, but that is distinct from the theorem's truth-smoothness hypothesis. The local type-S theorem supplies a separate direct argument for the broader Gaussian range; the definition should distinguish that local extension from what the cited source theorem states.

seams_checked.note: Opened the prerequisite page and the negative-Sobolev definition, bounded-Lipschitz lemma, density-normal series lemma, white-noise Gaussian lemma, and product-prior weak BvM theorem. The scalar consumers preserve the supplied posterior-kernel, prior-density, truth, topology, and countable-choice hypotheses. They use continuous linear pushforwards of bounded-Lipschitz convergence, without claiming an L² Gaussian limit or infinite-dimensional total-variation convergence.

Opened the prerequisite page and its bounded-variance Bernstein lemma. The actual direct use is the bounded independent-sum tail inequality in the type-S empirical coefficient bounds, with the variance and envelope checked locally. The current density proofs do not assert that the general entropy/prior-mass theorem automatically verifies their source-specific contraction premises; type-S contraction is proved locally and type H uses conjugacy.

Opened the prerequisite page, credible-set definition, measurable posterior quantile lemma, and equal-tailed interval theorem. Consumers preserve graph measurability and the posterior-mass-at-least convention. Quantile stabilization and frequentist coverage are established separately rather than attributed to posterior credibility alone.
